anomalies.obs: The ATO solenoid-valve low-side switch is implemented with T6 = AO3400A, a 30 V / SOT-23 small-signal N-MOSFET (drain on NET0073 to the 24 V valve load V2 DIGITEN-24V, gate on NET0065 driven via R32 100R from the T5 BT3904 level shifter).
anomalies.expected: The specification designates the ATO-valve switch as T3 = AON6407, a 60 V / 8-DFN N-MOSFET ('T3 — AON6407 (8-DFN N-MOSFET) ATO solenoid-valve low-side switch ... drives ATO_VALVE net; gate driven through R10 (100 Ω), pre-driven via T4 (BT3904)'). The level-shifter topology matches, but the power MOSFET itself is the wrong part.

evidence.quote: Sheet 2 (page F): 'T6 AO3400A' as the valve MOSFET, drain to NET0073 / H11 / P9 / V2 DIGITEN-24V, gate to NET0065 via R32 100R, source to GND
§2 Component Table: 'T3 — AON6407 (8-DFN N-MOSFET) | ATO solenoid-valve low-side switch'

anomalies.impact: The valve switch is a 30 V part on a 24 V inductive load (intended 60 V AON6407). With only the SS34 flyback clamp, Vds sits near 24 V with little headroom for transients, and Rds(on) is far higher than the specified device, so the valve driver is over-stressed and may fail/overheat — a deviation from the intended robust design (likely a sourcing/assembly substitution).

parsed.summary: The power train, isolators, TMC2209 dosing drivers, I2C/float interfaces and main-pump switch all match the intended architecture (reference-designator and auto-net-name differences, the unwired-vs-wired LiDAR, DNP environmental sensors and the firmware/schematic pin mismatch are documented spec properties, not anomalies). The one drawing-supported deviation is the ATO solenoid-valve low-side switch, built with a 30 V AO3400A instead of the specified 60 V AON6407.
